needs.premise: Exact header tuple read/CAS, close race, spent roles, late CAS and old release; role/actor assignment, VM lifetime and last-write release external; finite sampling not native proof.
Selective gate closure, spent-role, idempotent release, generation identity and writer coverage laws; not complete QNT/C induction.
Future generated SFUN/CFUN/catcher and thread exit must settle exact last writes, borrows and cleanup debt before releasing roles; present first patch adds no such callers.

Candidates pre-recorded before CAS; bounded exclusive actors 1..255 and one producer per role; no processor-id shortcut or destroyed-VM query. Identity allocator and result journal are not implemented here.

Full header CAS contains tag, closed, spent/live bits; source uses existing full-barrier backend. Encoding injectivity, emulation/platform ordering and compiler qualification remain open; sequential backend only without sharing.

64 fixed VM records initialize before processor exposure. No Scheme payload/root scanning. All access requires live VM storage borrow; cleanup/router drain and repeated setup lifetime are separate gates.

First patch installs source primitive/build/test target and VM initialization only. Marker pre-root, nonzero processor root scan, generated exit funnel and lifecycle closure precede activation of managed callers.

Inherit 8/12 repairs. Replace constructor/rollback/pending join/old-handler custody with canonical membership transactions and real stop/drain receipts. MC-SCOPE is necessary authority support, not native recovery evidence.

RootRegistry/FrameSpec, marker-before-allocation root protection, typed constructor publication and participating native entry must replace actual implicit consumers. C gate has no Scheme root fields and proves none of this.

Existing stdlib invalid type read has unresolved corruption/structure/error-reporting alternatives. Trace concrete producer and root/writer violation before selecting a repair; stable native scope alone cannot prove cause or cure.

Numerical generated-C compile deadline and release latency/build consumers need separate compiler/build/runtime work decomposition and matched unchanged gates. No causal dependency from a passing gate primitive to faster compilation.

Successor requires previous helper generation control/data closure, no delayed operations or writers, exact lease and drained metadata readers; never reuse original owner receipt or replay root/native effects.

Keep pending root cell safe false; old frozen source view covers GC until canonical root-admission accepts current value. Slot owns initialized scan contract before close; final commit publishes only control after full root/metadata validation.

Entry gate and in-flight acquisition must be one race-safe protocol; release close receipt follows actual stores, acquire exact generation precedes handoff. Plain field exclusivity and platform stop remain open.

architecture.lesson: PVM paper: front/back cooperation exposes representation, calls and target knowledge
architecture.replacement: Scheme owns FrameSpec/PointId/ModuleSpec/EffectSpec/AllocationSpec; generate typed C functions/tables and explicit ABI
architecture.retirement: Retire duplicated semantic macro emission and layout decisions after all generators/runtime consumers use the schema
architecture.obligation: Prove complete encoding, decoding, root coverage, tail/non-tail and continuation origins; existing fragments are insufficient
architecture.benefit: Count repeated preprocessing/compile bytes and semantic decisions eliminated; no new language runtime required
architecture.addedCost: Schema/compiler bootstrap cost and an ABI rebuild; simple C portability macros may remain

architecture.target: Execution, participation and collection carriers separated
architecture.lesson: OCaml parallelism paper and domain/backup-thread source: GC participation is an explicit protocol
architecture.replacement: VM owns membership/heap epochs; ExecutionContext owns Scheme state; GCParticipant freezes roots; CollectorWorkContext owns scan work independent of OS/PSTATE lifetime
architecture.retirement: Retire implicit PSTATE ownership of collector queues, allocation state and cleanup after exact producer/consumer/lifetime replacement
architecture.obligation: Compose safepoint progress, membership closure, root leases and task termination; exclude collector/owner wait cycles
architecture.benefit: Reduce owner-dependent GC callbacks and repeated membership reconstruction; measure contention and pause population
architecture.addedCost: Root snapshots, epoch bookkeeping and scheduler/worker coordination; no universal dead-thread recovery

architecture.target: Generational heap with precise publication and mutation
architecture.lesson: OCaml paper compares concurrent minor/read-barrier design with parallel STW minor; learn the tradeoff
architecture.replacement: Context-local nurseries, shared mature heap, parallel STW minor, generated remembered writes and explicit promotion budget; isolate major algorithm behind heap/phase contract
architecture.retirement: Retire full mature-graph minor scanning only after all roots, continuation/denv/FFI writers and sparse/promotion layouts close
architecture.obligation: Prove no omitted mature-to-young edge, root-complete minor cut, promotion failure custody and capacity conservation
architecture.benefit: Minor work = young live + remembered edges + roots; savings require avoiding mature scan beyond barrier/promotion overhead
architecture.addedCost: Remembered sets, barriers, survival/promotion copies and reserve peaks; mature moving/nonmoving and concurrent major remain open choices

architecture.lesson: Effects paper makes suspension/resumption a runtime concern; Gambit already has stronger multi-shot semantics
architecture.replacement: One precise frame/root format for running, captured and resumed computation; persistent or copy-on-write captured frames; one-shot optimization only with proven use
architecture.retirement: Retire carrier-local C control assumptions after repeated resumption, dynamic-wind, exceptions and supported FFI escapes are preserved
architecture.obligation: Capture map continuation, collect/promote, mutate legal frames/denv and resume more than once with same observable semantics
architecture.benefit: Reuse captured immutable graph across minor GC only with complete mutation evidence; direct-style scheduling without rewriting Scheme
architecture.addedCost: Frame ownership/COW bookkeeping, remembered mutations and handler/FFI boundary cost; do not impose one-shot restriction

architecture.target: Root-safe native activation and effect/resource ownership
architecture.lesson: OCaml source separates blocking leave/reenter and GC service; Gambit needs its own continuation-aware contract
architecture.replacement: RootRegistry before allocation; generated native entry plans; park/freeze/reload; VM-owned outcomes and effect-classified release tasks outside collector critical phase
architecture.retirement: Retire raw marker-only lifetime, ad hoc root choreography and inline arbitrary release only after whole real caller coverage
architecture.obligation: Compose nested callback, exact last use, late result, exception/continuation escape and release descendants with GC progress
architecture.benefit: Remove duplicated per-entry ownership logic and avoid waiting for blocked owner in collector phase
architecture.addedCost: Stable roots, task custody, resource affinity and root-aware resumption; unknown unregistered writers still require refusal/retention

architecture.target: Semantic artifact graph and native compilation boundary
architecture.lesson: PVM separation plus existing build research: interface programs and dependency-aware products, not command wrappers
architecture.replacement: Scheme frontend/session -> semantic module artifacts -> generated C/runtime ABI artifacts; phase-ready dependency DAG, stable snapshots, incremental/parallel scheduling and reusable AOT interface programs
architecture.retirement: Retire repeated expansion and regenerated/recompiled unaffected units after clean-versus-incremental observational equivalence
architecture.obligation: Prove dynamic dependency closure, stable input snapshot, output encoding/consumer reflection and failure invalidation
architecture.benefit: Unchanged/leaf/macro-change work counts; whole build latency and C parser work under existing caps
architecture.addedCost: Dependency/snapshot storage, artifact validation and unavoidable state instantiation; LLVM/MLIR adapters consume contracts, Zig optional

candidate.reason: MC-SCOPE is an isolated inactive candidate primitive. Fixed roles, actor id, generation and slot capacity must not become arbitrary restrictions on Scheme/FFI semantics. No further activation is justified by its commit or finite model alone.

canonicalModules.label: Scheme semantic planner
canonicalModules.owns: Normalization, GVM semantic completion, effects, FrameSpec, PointId and primitive/FFI legality
canonicalModules.provides: Closed semantic plan and ordered module contract
canonicalModules.excludes: Does not choose execution scheduling or native resource ownership

canonicalModules.label: Modern generated C
canonicalModules.owns: Mechanical lowering and generated frame/root/layout/entry declarations from completed plan
canonicalModules.provides: C ABI, trampoline and exact layout adapters
canonicalModules.excludes: Does not invent a second Scheme semantic policy

canonicalModules.label: VM and execution admission
canonicalModules.owns: Execution grants, park/reentry, participant membership, resize and exit admission
canonicalModules.provides: Stable context identity with explicit join/leave and last-user closure
canonicalModules.excludes: A descriptor or published TLS pointer is not an execution grant

canonicalModules.label: Root and lifetime interface
canonicalModules.owns: Cross-owner root-cut, slot-update and last-reader agreement; execution/FFI remain value custodians, GC remains scanner
canonicalModules.provides: Epoch-bound root slots and scan grants with reload obligations
canonicalModules.excludes: Does not take semantic ownership away from producer and scanner modules

canonicalModules.label: Allocation and collection
canonicalModules.owns: Heap layout, allocation budgets, copy/scan tasks, phases, promotion and reclaim decisions
canonicalModules.provides: Complete work context with parent/child/Tail custody and phase closure
canonicalModules.excludes: Worker identity does not imply processor or native-thread identity

canonicalModules.label: Continuation and dynamic control
canonicalModules.owns: Captured/current/saved frame interpretation, denv mutation, restore and supported nonlocal exits
canonicalModules.provides: Root-complete frame traversal and resumption origins
canonicalModules.excludes: Gambit continuations are not silently restricted to one-shot effect resumptions

canonicalModules.label: Foreign entry and blocking
canonicalModules.owns: Borrow scopes, root protection before marker allocation, nested callback origin and acquired-effect cleanup
canonicalModules.provides: Admitted host entry, block transition and explicit result/control boundary
canonicalModules.excludes: Raw C pointers do not survive moving GC by language interoperability alone

canonicalModules.label: Resource release coordination
canonicalModules.owns: Classified release effects, thread-affine jobs, WaitContext, derived-task accounting and shutdown drain
canonicalModules.provides: Accepted task custody and exactly owned completion/result disposition
canonicalModules.excludes: A drained GC phase is not proof that external resources or borrowers drained

canonicalModules.label: Incremental build engine and artifact graph
canonicalModules.owns: Rule planning, dependencies, rebuild decision, CPU/memory scheduling and transactional artifact publication
canonicalModules.provides: Source/plan/generated/object/link lineage and effective multicore ABI
canonicalModules.excludes: Does not define Scheme unit semantics or count build threads as runtime processors
